sources.title: First Data for NKTR-214 in Combination with OPDIVO (nivolumab) for Patients with Stage IV Melanoma, Renal Cell Carcinoma and Non-Small Cell Lung Cancers, Including Patients with PD-L1 Negative Status, Revealed at SITC 2017

excerpts.text: 38 patients enrolled across multiple dose cohorts. Melanoma (Stage IV, treatment-naive): 7/11 efficacy-evaluable patients responded (63%), 2 complete responses, 5 partial responses, disease control rate 91%. Renal cell carcinoma (treatment-naive), two or more scans: 6/10 patients (60%), 1 CR, 5 PR, disease control 85%. Renal cell carcinoma (2L, I-O naive): 1/7 patients (14%), 1 PR, disease control 100%. NSCLC (2L, PD-L1 negative): 3/4 patients (75%), 1 CR, 2 PR.

Recommended Phase 2 dose: NKTR-214 0.006 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks plus Opdivo (nivolumab) 360 mg IV every 3 weeks. Most common grade 1-2 adverse events: fatigue 74%, flu-like symptoms 68%, rash 60%, pruritus 42%. No grade 3+ immune-mediated adverse events at RP2D or below; no treatment discontinuations due to adverse events; no study deaths.

Robust expansion of ICOS+ CD4 and CD8+ T cells in the blood and increased ICOS gene expression in the tumor observed with combination therapy. Phase 2 expansion actively enrolling across 5 tumor types in approximately 330 patients (melanoma, renal cell carcinoma, NSCLC, bladder, triple-negative breast cancer).

sources.title: Lilly and Nektar Therapeutics Announce Alliance to Develop and Commercialize NKTR-358, A Novel Autoimmune Therapy

excerpts.text: Upfront payment of $150 million to Nektar; up to $250 million in additional development and regulatory milestones. Phase 2 cost-sharing: 75% Lilly, 25% Nektar; Nektar has option to participate in Phase 3 on an indication-by-indication basis and is eligible for double-digit royalties that increase commensurate with its Phase 3 investment and product sales. Nektar completes Phase 1; Lilly leads Phase 2 and later development and commercialization. NKTR-358 achieved first human dose in Phase 1 clinical development in March 2017; targets the IL-2 receptor complex to stimulate regulatory T cells for autoimmune and chronic inflammatory conditions.

sources.title: NKTR-181 Meets Primary and Secondary Endpoints in Phase 3 SUMMIT-07 Study in Chronic Pain

excerpts.text: SUMMIT-07 randomized more than 600 patients with moderate-to-severe chronic low back pain, new to opioid therapy, comparing twice-daily NKTR-181 tablets to placebo. Met primary efficacy endpoint of improved chronic back pain relief versus placebo (p=0.0019); key secondary endpoints also met with high statistical significance, including more favorable sleep outcomes on the Medical Outcomes Study Sleep Scale.

claims.text: Under the February 2018 collaboration agreement, the partner pays an upfront $1.0 billion cash plus an $850 million equity investment (8,284,600 shares at $102.60/share), with up to $1.78 billion in additional development, regulatory and sales milestones, and the companies split worldwide commercialization profit 65% (Nektar) / 35% (BMS).

The joint clinical development plan covers more than 20 indications across 9 tumor types, combining the candidate with the partner's approved PD-1 checkpoint inhibitor and with that inhibitor plus a CTLA-4 inhibitor; pivotal studies in renal cell carcinoma and melanoma are expected to begin in mid-2018.
The companies expected to complete the collaboration transaction during the second quarter of 2018, subject to antitrust clearance.

In a 38-patient dose-escalation study, objective response rates were 63% (7/11) in treatment-naive stage IV melanoma, 60% (6/10) in treatment-naive stage IV renal cell carcinoma with 2+ scans, 14% (1/7) in previously treated renal cell carcinoma, and 75% (3/4) in PD-L1-negative previously treated non-small cell lung cancer.

The recommended Phase 2 dose was the candidate at 0.006 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks with the partner's checkpoint inhibitor at 360 mg IV every 3 weeks; the most common adverse events were low-grade (fatigue 74%, flu-like symptoms 68%, rash 60%, pruritus 42%), with no grade 3-or-higher immune-mediated adverse events at or below the recommended dose, no discontinuations for adverse events, and no deaths on study.

Biomarker analyses showed expansion of certain T-cell populations in blood and an immune-activation gene-expression marker in tumor tissue; a roughly 330-patient dose-expansion phase across 5 tumor types was already enrolling as of this data.
Third-quarter 2017 revenue of $152.9 million was driven primarily by recognition of $125.9 million from an unrelated new collaboration's upfront license payment, received in September 2017.

At September 30, 2017: cash and cash equivalents were $38.0 million, short-term investments $314.6 million and long-term investments $59.6 million (total $412.2 million); debt totaled $253.0 million ($250.0 million of 7.75% senior secured notes due October 2020 plus $3.0 million of capital lease obligations, with a $60.0 million minimum cash/investments covenant); shares outstanding were 157,467,703 as of November 2, 2017.
Nine-month 2017 net cash from operating activities was essentially breakeven ($13 thousand) versus a $64.6 million outflow in the same period of 2016.

The company's own filing describes 'significant and escalating double-digit royalty payments' plus sales milestones on the opioid-induced-constipation drug's worldwide net sales (with a separate regional licensee paying the company 40% of its own royalty stream), and a $10.0 million EU-approval milestone plus sales milestones and royalties (rate undisclosed) on the hemophilia drug.

Under a mid-2017 agreement, the autoimmune-disease-candidate partner paid $150 million upfront, with up to $250 million in additional milestones and double-digit royalties that increase with the company's own Phase 3 investment; the company completes Phase 1 while the partner funds 75% of Phase 2 and leads later development; the candidate achieved its first human dose in Phase 1 in March 2017.

The chronic-pain candidate's Phase 3 SUMMIT-07 study (more than 600 opioid-naive patients with moderate-to-severe chronic low back pain) met its primary endpoint (pain relief versus placebo, p=0.0019) and key secondary endpoints, including sleep-quality measures, with high statistical significance; topline results were announced in March 2017 and full data presented in September 2017.
The company will book all worldwide sales and revenue for the lead oncology candidate and retains final decision-making authority on its pricing.

Development costs for combination trials are shared based on relative ownership: for the candidate with the partner's PD-1 inhibitor alone, the partner bears 67.5% and the company 32.5%; for the triplet with the PD-1 and CTLA-4 inhibitors, the partner bears 78% and the company 22%; the company is solely responsible for manufacturing.

The company describes itself as a research-based biopharmaceutical company that leverages a proprietary chemistry platform to discover and design new drug candidates, and states that its working capital is expected to fund its current business plans for at least the next twelve months.
Nine-month 2017 operating margin was about -16.8% (operating loss of $35.6 million divided by revenue of $212.2 million), versus about -63.1% in the same period of 2016.
Net cash, investments and debt at September 30, 2017 was approximately $159.2 million ($412.2 million cash and investments minus $253.0 million of total debt).
Excluding the approximately $125.9 million one-time license-revenue item, underlying third-quarter 2017 revenue was approximately $27.0 million.
